arms.query: At Lumen Wharf, why was the Tide pilot delayed, who owns its revised schedule, and what condition must be met before it starts?

sources.content:
Mara Venn owns the revised Tide pilot schedule. She coordinates dates with
the harbor crew but does not control the instrument test itself.

For routine handoffs, open the checklist, mark the items already reviewed, and
leave the remainder for the next shift. The checklist is a record of work in
progress, not an authorization to change the underlying arrangement. Staff can
add a short note when a handoff crosses a weekend or a public holiday.

The Tide pilot was moved back because the shore sensors produced
inconsistent readings after salt spray. The team chose to retest the
instruments before inviting the first vessels.

To prepare the shared working folder, staff place the latest notes beside the intake
sheet and retain the previous copy in the archive. A coordinator checks the file
name and the date before the next handoff. If a document is missing, the team
records that gap and asks for the original; a replacement is not assumed to exist.

The Tide pilot can start once three consecutive salt-spray trials pass
calibration. A calendar date has not yet been committed.

The office keeps a separate log for day-to-day questions. Each entry contains the
date received and a brief description, followed by the initials of the person
who filed it. Entries are reviewed in batches, and outdated drafts stay labeled
as drafts until someone supplies a verified replacement.

arms.query: For Mosaic Orchard’s frost alert service, what triggers an alert, where is it sent, and what action is the grower expected to take?

sources.content:
The service sends a frost alert to the grower’s registered phone by text
message. The dashboard stores a copy but does not substitute for the text.

For routine handoffs, open the checklist, mark the items already reviewed, and
leave the remainder for the next shift. The checklist is a record of work in
progress, not an authorization to change the underlying arrangement. Staff can
add a short note when a handoff crosses a weekend or a public holiday.

After receiving an alert, the grower is expected to inspect the irrigation
valves before deciding whether to run sprinklers. The service does not turn
the valves on.

The frost alert is triggered when the orchard probe records two readings
below 1°C at least ten minutes apart. A single low reading alone does not
trigger it.
